data.exact_reserve_text: During 2024 the Syndicate released $47.7m of technical reserves in respect of prior years (2023: $89.2m), arising predominantly from the Treaty, Property and Casualty divisions (2023: Casualty, Marine and Treaty divisions). These releases were due to favourable claims development on prior year losses during 2024, partially offset by reserve strengthening on Political Risk and Violence. Refer to Note 19 for further details.

prior_year_events.impact_description: The Syndicate has material exposure to claims arising from the Russia and Ukraine crisis; the current estimated ultimate claims are $380.3m gross (2023: $285.3m) and $193.3m net of reinsurance. After allowing for inwards and outwards reinstatement premiums this increases to $209.1m.

The Syndicate has exposure to losses emanating from the Covid-19 pandemic. The current estimated ultimate claims are $151.6m gross (2023: $160.1m) and $103.4m net of reinsurance. After allowing for inwards and outwards reinstatement premiums this reduces to $99.5m.

data.standardized_narrative: At 1 January 2024 the Syndicate's gross claims outstanding were $3,416.9m. During 2024 the Syndicate recorded a net release in prior year claims estimates; the claims provisions note shows a gross reduction in prior year provisions of $25.782m (a circa 0.75% release of opening gross claims outstanding). Management attributes the favourable movement predominantly to favourable claims development on prior year losses, partly offset by reserve strengthening related to Political Risk/Violence and exposures arising from the Russia/Ukraine crisis and other large man-made losses. Material named events cited in the reserves note for 2024 include Dubai flooding, Hurricanes Helene and Milton, Typhoon Yagi, Calgary hailstorms and the Baltimore bridge collapse, with quantified gross estimates provided for some events.

data.data_quality_notes: All monetary values are reported in the report's native currency (USD) and converted to millions. The prior year movement used is the gross 'Change in estimates of prior year provisions' line from Note 19 (-$25,782k = -25.782m). The narrative in the segmental analysis refers to released technical reserves of $47.7m which appears to reconcile a broader technical reserve measure (or different aggregation) than the claims-only prior year movement in Note 19; users should note this difference. Exchange rate movements and inclusion/exclusion of reinstatement premiums may also cause differences between narrative and table amounts.
